
=== story.oldMillRoad ===
TRIAL 26 CRS 005000 · State of North Carolina v. Belinda Park
  Charges: Felony Death by Vehicle; Reckless Driving
  Defendant: Belinda Park, 29, Line cook; priors: 0; Released on a $225,000 secured bond with electronic monitoring.
  TEMPLATE story.oldMillRoad
  Summary: At about 11:52 p.m. on 25 December, Belinda Park's Honda Civic crossed the center line on a curve on Old Mill Road outside Bayard and struck a Toyota Corolla head-on. The Corolla's driver, Alex Fitzgerald, 34, a nurse driving home from a twelve-hour shift, died at the scene. Belinda Park, a line cook at Riverside Grill, had stayed after closing that night. A hospital blood test about ninety minutes after the crash and a second, State Crime Laboratory test about three hours after it disagree on whether Park was over the legal limit when the cars collided. Park says a deer came out of the tree line and she swerved.
  Verdicts: Felony Death by Vehicle: notGuilty; Reckless Driving: guilty
  [Count 2: Reckless Driving] Class 2 Misdemeanor, prior conviction level I | Presumptive range | 10 days, suspended. Community punishment: 12 months of probation.
  [Conditions of probation] Regular conditions of probation under G.S. 15A-1343(b) apply. | Supervised probation: report as directed, submit to warrantless searches by the probation officer, remain within the jurisdiction.
  [Monetary obligations] Court costs: US$213.00 | Restitution: US$15,000.00 | Appointed attorney fees: US$1,600.00 | Attorney appointment fee: US$60.00 | State Crime Laboratory fee: US$600.00 | Supervision fees ($40/month): US$480.00 | Total: US$17,953.00
  [Victim notification] The District Attorney's victim-witness legal assistant will notify the victim of the judgment and of any release, appeal, or post-conviction hearing (N.C. Const. art. I, § 37).
  Reaction: District Attorney Perla Edmondson: "We're grateful to the officers and witnesses who saw this case through."
  Reaction: Leonora Yow: "The court saw a person, not just a file. We're grateful."
  Reaction: Alex Fitzgerald's father, outside the courtroom: "We'll be watching to make sure every condition is followed."
  News: Guilty: Park case ends in conviction — A Hollis County judge has convicted Belinda Park on 1 of 2 counts of reckless driving, and imposed a suspended sentence and 12 months of probation. At about 11:52 p.m. on 25 December, Belinda Park's Honda Civic crossed the center line on a curve on Old Mill Road outside Bayard and struck a Toyota Corolla head-on. Two groups gathered on opposite sides of the courthouse steps. Leonora Yow: "The court saw a person, not just a file. We're grateful." Alex Fitzgerald's father, outside the courtroom: "We'll be watching to make sure every condition is followed." District Attorney Perla Edmondson: "We're grateful to the officers and witnesses who saw this case through." Park left the courthouse with family. TRIAL 26 CRS 005010 · State of North Carolina v. Antonia Beaumont
  Charges: Embezzlement ($100,000 or more)
  Defendant: Antonia Beaumont, 46, School bus mechanic; priors: 14; Held in the Hollis County jail on a $250,000 secured bond for 74 days.
  TEMPLATE story.churchBooks
  Summary: For six years Antonia Beaumont, a school bus mechanic for Hollis County Schools, served as the volunteer treasurer of Cedar Hill United Methodist Church in Wexley. When a new trustee asked for the building fund statements, $112,400 was gone, moved over three years in 41 checks and transfers to an account in the name of "DL Property Services." Beaumont says Pastor Harold Peebles approved every payment as short-term loans to the contractor rebuilding the fellowship hall, and that the paperwork was handshakes. The pastor, now retired and in poor health, says no such arrangement existed.
  Verdicts: Embezzlement ($100,000 or more): guilty
  [Count 1: Embezzlement ($100,000 or more)] Class C Felony, prior record level VI | Presumptive range | Minimum 117, maximum 153 months. Active: committed to the custody of the N.C. Department of Adult Correction.
  [Commitment] Minimum term to be served before the defendant is eligible for release: 117 months (9 yr 9 mo). | Maximum term: 153 months. Earned time can move release toward the minimum, never below it; post-release supervision follows release. | Credit for 74 days already served in pretrial confinement (G.S. 15-196.1). | Projected release: no earlier than 5 June 2036, and no later than 5 June 2038. | Upon release, the defendant will serve a period of post-release supervision (G.S. 15A-1368.2).
  [Monetary obligations] Court costs: US$213.00 | Total: US$213.00
  Reaction: ADA Ada Wooten: "This is a fair result under the sentencing laws, and it's about public trust."
  Reaction: Rita Bradsher: "It's a hard day. We'll be talking with Beaumont about next steps."
  Reaction: A relative of Beaumont's: "We'll be waiting when it's over."
  News: Verdict in ‘$112,000 and a Handshake’ case: guilty — Superior Court Judge Hale found Antonia Beaumont, 46, guilty, and imposed 117 to 153 months in prison, ending a case that began with an arrest in Wexley. According to court records, for six years Antonia Beaumont, a school bus mechanic for Hollis County Schools, served as the volunteer treasurer of Cedar Hill United Methodist Church in Wexley. Reaction outside the courthouse was split. A relative of Beaumont's: "We'll be waiting when it's over." ADA Ada Wooten: "This is a fair result under the sentencing laws, and it's about public trust." Rita Bradsher: "It's a hard day. We'll be talking with Beaumont about next steps." Deputies led Beaumont out a side door. Counting 74 days already served, the earliest possible release is 5 June 2036.

Lucas says Hedgepeth came at Lucas with the skillet after a night of drinking and she grabbed Hedgepeth to stop it.   Charges: First-Degree Murder; Forgery of an Instrument; Uttering a Forged Instrument; Insurance Fraud
  Defendant: Xiomara Goldberg, 38, Pharmacy technician; priors: 0; Held without bond in the Hollis County jail for 39 days.
  TEMPLATE story.eyeDropPoisoning
  Summary: On 21 June, Xiomara Goldberg called 911 to report that her husband, Darren Herring, had fallen down the stairs of their home in Port Hollis. Paramedics found Herring dead at the bottom of the steps. The medical examiner first called it an accident. A routine toxicology screen, sent out because Herring had a heart condition, came back with tetrahydrozoline at many times a therapeutic level, the decongestant in over-the-counter eye drops. Swallowed, it slows the heart and drops blood pressure. Over the next month, Goldberg wrote herself $41,000 in checks from Herring's account and filed a life insurance claim. Goldberg first told police Herring had been depressed, then later said she had put drops in his water over three days to make him sick, not to kill him.

Damon Eze, the pledge master who organized the gauntlet, is one of several brothers charged. Someone deleted footage from the cameras after the death; the police recovered it.

The district attorney charged first-degree murder, saying the law doesn't allow anyone to decide another person's life is not worth living.
